subject: Dedicated capacity intake — NeuxAI sizing inputs
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <alex@neuxai.com>
Cc: Priya Chandrasekhar <priya@neuxai.com>
Date: 2029-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity intake — NeuxAI sizing inputs

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. To make our Dedicated sizing accurate I need a short traffic/profile dump from your side — the fields below will help us map to GPU SKUs and recommended commit. If you can drop answers / example traces (CSV preferred) that would be ideal.

Quick ask (it should take ~15-20 minutes):
- Expected steady-state RPS (per-region) and p95 burst rate (per-hour/day).
- Average prompt length (tokens) and average generated response length (tokens).
- Typical session duration and whether you re-use KV cache / streaming sessions.
- Percent of requests that are chat (multi-turn) vs single-turn completion.
- SLA targets (p99 latency goal, e.g., <300ms) and any required SLAs for tail latency.
- Peak concurrency window (how many concurrent users/threads at peak minute).
- Any offline batch/embeddings peaks that need dedicated GPUs.

I attached our redwood_dedicated_sizing_form_v2.pdf — if you prefer, just send a CSV with per-minute traces for a sample day.

Once we have that, I’ll run a preliminary capacity model and come back with a recommended GPU sku mix and suggested reserved capacity (and an optional canary path).

Can we also lock a quick 30-min follow-up on Thurs to review? I dropped a booking link below.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soogin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_dedicated_sizing_form_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Alex Ramos <alex@neuxai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Chandrasekhar <priya@neuxai.com>
Date: 2029-04-10T11:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake — NeuxAI sizing inputs

On 2029-04-10 09:12, Soojin Lee wrote:
> Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. To make our Dedicated sizing accurate I need a short traffic/profile dump from your side — the fields below will help us map to GPU SKUs and recommended commit. If you can drop answers / example traces (CSV preferred) that would be ideal.

Thanks Soojin — attaching a short export from our production telemetry and our SLA doc. High-level answers inline below and full CSV attached.

- Steady-state RPS: 18 RPS US-east, 4 RPS EU. Peak p95 burst: 210 RPS during marketing campaign spikes (approx 2–3 hours once per week).
- Average prompt length: 45 tokens. Average response: 160 tokens (we do truncation at 512 but ~95% are <300).
- Session duration: median session ~75s; ~22% of sessions involve 3+ turns and reuse of session KV cache.
- Chat vs single-turn: ~35% chat multi-turn, 65% single-turn completions.
- SLA targets: p99 < 600ms for interactive flows; non-critical batch latency ok to be higher. Tail spikes we need graceful fallback (lower fidelity model) rather than failure.
- Peak concurrency window: about 380 concurrent sessions at campaign peak minute.
- Embeddings/batch: nightly embeddings job peaks at 12:30 UTC (~4 concurrent jobs, each GPU-heavy for ~30 min).

Files attached: neuxai_sample_telemetry_2029Q1.csv, sla_requirements_neuxai.pdf

Happy to jump on Thurs.

—Alex
Ops Lead, NeuxAI
[attachment: neuxai_sample_telemetry_2029Q1.csv (csv)]
[attachment: sla_requirements_neuxai.pdf (pdf)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-10T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity intake — NeuxAI sizing inputs

Forwarding Alex's telemetry and SLA. Key signals: 380 concurrent peak sessions, 210 RPS marketing peaks, avg response ~160 tokens, 22% multi-turn sessions. They want p99 <600ms and graceful fallback.

Quick notes / ask from pre-sales sizing POV:
- Preliminary thought: consider 8x A100-80GB equivalent slots for steady + 2–3 burst nodes (or mix with cheaper 80GB/40GB Ampere gen for non-chat flows). Will run exact token-based cost model.
- Need a mapping from their per-minute trace => session concurrency profile to convert to model tokens/sec per GPU. Ben, can you run the "tokenized throughput" sim against our 2 candidate SKUs (A100-like / H100-like) and return: recommended min reserved vGPU count, expected p99 under continuous 18RPS baseline, and burst headroom for 210 RPS?
- Marissa, can you prepare a quick CAN/TSLA-style proposal with the canary plan (10% canary on launch + automatic downgrade to smaller model when queue > X)?

I compiled a brief summary sheet attached. If it's easier, I can also run a first-pass model and share numbers before Ben runs the sim.

Thanks — would like to have a draft recommendation before Thurs call.

Soogin
[attachment: neuxai_telemetry_summary.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <alex@neuxai.com>
Cc: Priya Chandrasekhar <priya@neuxai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-12T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity intake — NeuxAI sizing inputs

Alex — thanks for the fast turnaround and the CSV. We reviewed the traces and outlined the next steps below: 

1) Internal modeling: Ben will run tokenized throughput sims (A100-like & H100-like) and deliver an initial reserved capacity recommendation by EOD tomorrow.
2) Canary + fallback: Marissa will draft a canary plan (10% traffic) and a queue-length-based fallback that routes to a lower-cost model when queue growth exceeds a threshold.
3) Follow-up review: locked a 30-min review slot — booking link: https://cal.com/redwood/30min?event=neuxai-sizing. Please confirm if Thurs 11:00 PT works.

We expect to surface: recommended reserved GPU count, suggested SKU mix, estimated monthly committed cost, and a short runbook for graceful degradation.

If there are any special compliance or VPC/on-prem constraints, let me know and we’ll fold that into the plan. Looking forward to the call.

Best,
Soogin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
